chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Mus'ab, from Sa'd ibn Turaif, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, blessings of Allah be upon them both, that he said:
"Deal gently with the hypocrite using your tongue, and be sincere in your love for the believer, and if a Jew were to sit with you, then be gracious in his company."

key_terms.الْمُنَافِقَ: the hypocrite, one who conceals disbelief

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about how to treat hypocrites, believers, and non-Muslims?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) instructs on maintaining proper social conduct with people of different faiths and levels of sincerity. The teaching distinguishes between diplomatic courtesy toward hypocrites, genuine love for fellow believers, and basic human decency toward non-Muslims. This hadith was delivered in the context of a diverse early Muslim society where Shia communities navigated relationships with hypocrites within the Muslim community and People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) in their neighbourhoods.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 10. And with the preceding chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Mas’ab, from Sa’d ibn Turaif, from: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon both, who said:
"Soften your speech with [even] the hypocrite, love the faithful believer sincerely, and [even] if a Jew were to sit with you, then be gracious in his company."
